hypothesis: A prompt chunk's input projections spend host time the card makes redundant: the batched attention quantizes the whole chunk on the host for wq_a and wkv although both run on their mirrors and never read that copy (1.5 s over the 3.3k prompt), normalizes the query item by item on one thread, and makes the compressor's and the indexer-compressor's four bf16 projections in two calls, each uploading the chunk again and syncing. Skipping the unused copy, spreading the norm over the OpenMP threads and making the four projections in one device call (one upload, one sync, a kernel that reads each input once for four rows in the same order) shortens the time to the first token, with the same bits.
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 architecture, abliterated weights (same shapes), safetensors, native FP8/FP4
command: make -C c -f Makefile.deepseek-v4 deepseek-v4 CUDA=1 DEEPGEMM=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.3 ARCH=native; deepseek_v4 <model> --prompt-file prompt3k.txt --max-tokens 36 --memory-gb 16 with the environment in config; the arms alternate (baseline, trial) three times on one binary; tok_s = 3278 prompt tokens / time_to_first_token from the engine's `timing` line (prompt throughput)

hardware.storage: Samsung 990 PRO 4TB + 980 PRO 2TB NVMe in one LVM volume, ext4, direct aligned reads

quality.method: greedy text identical across the arm's runs and identical to the trial's (md5 of stdout)
